rv.q: This ship of dreams really is unsinkable.
Hysterical, knowingly corny and as frothy as sea foam, Tye Blue’s production has a fantastically brash, devil-may-care spirit and sparkling performances.
Equally, on its own terms, guying epic cinema with a shoestring theatricality, it’s hard to fault.
There is nothing subtle about this jukebox musical, and that’s what makes it so glorious.
But by the end, the cumulative effect is irresistible, especially when delivered by a cast so sharply on their game and possessed of such blazing voices.
The whole thing is infectiously silly albeit overlong; when the tempo drops, the effect on the production overall is worryingly noticeable.
Camp and chaotic musical burlesque of the movie Titanic that hits all the right notes
Only Drew and her Celine Dion character are really remarkable here, but it’s undeniably a fun way to start 2025.
Quite possibly the most fun you will ever have in a theatre, this may be the funniest show in the West End at the moment
If you’re in the mood for something silly, absurd, and utterly hilarious, this is the perfect pick for a night of irreverent fun and incredible musical performances.
It is very silly – relentlessly so, really – but resistance is ultimately futile.
For those willing to embrace its chaos and nostalgic charm, it’s an irresistible treat.
It’s neither Ibsen nor a celebrity star-signed crossgender Shakespeare but just screechingly camp fun.
Fun, frothy and outrageous, it may be just too silly for some, often feeling like going on some sort of psychedelic trip into the chaotically fevered mind of delirious panto dame.
That they are crude is fine, that they are devoid of wit isn’t.
